property_summary: Only the contract owner can successfully call setApprovedLogger; any non-owner call must revert.
Calls to setApprovedLogger revert for callers that are not the contract owner (i.e., non-owner callers cannot successfully execute setApprovedLogger).
Calling setApprovedLogger by a non-owner must revert (i.e., only the owner can call it successfully).
setApprovedLogger succeeds (does not revert) iff the caller is the contract owner.

Invariant: Only the contract owner can set approvedLoggers (i.e., calling setApprovedLogger from any non-owner must not change approvedLoggers); the mutant removes the onlyOwner guard so some caller can flip an approvedLoggers entry and thus violate this property.

In the reference C only the contract owner can change approvedLoggers, so for any caller x and any key k, if x is not the owner then calling approvedToLog(k) (a view) does not change approvedLoggers(k); the mutant removes onlyOwner from setApprovedLogger allowing some caller to change approvedLoggers(k) and thus violate this invariance for some fuzzed inputs.

Calling the read-only approvedToLog(address) view function must never alter any approvedLoggers mapping entry in the correct contract; the mutant (which removed onlyOwner from setApprovedLogger) allows some caller to change approvedLoggers and thus can make approvedLoggers(k) differ after such a call for some inputs.

property_summary: Only the contract owner can successfully call setApprovedLogger; calls from non-owner addresses must revert.

For any caller address, if logCreated is called by an approved logger it must emit the Created event (and return true); the mutant still returns true for approved callers but fails to emit the Created event, so it violates the rule for some approved caller addresses.

For every caller address that is approved via setApprovedLogger, calling logCreated(...) returns true and also causes the Created event to be emitted; the mutant still returns true for approved callers but does not emit the Created event, so it violates the rule for some approved caller.

For every caller address that is approved via setApprovedLogger, calling logCreated(...) returns true and emits the Created event; the mutant still returns true but fails to emit the Created event for some approved caller, violating this rule.

For any caller address that is approved via setApprovedLogger, calling logCreated(...) must both return true and emit the Created event; the mutant still returns true for approved callers but omits emitting Created for some approved caller addresses, violating this rule.

For every address addr that is approved via setApprovedLogger(addr, true), calling logCreated(...) from that addr returns true and emits the Created event (i.e. the call completes successfully and the Created event is observable); the mutant still returns true for approved callers but fails to emit the Created event for some approved caller, breaking this rule.

For every call to logRedemptionRequested, the reference contract returns true iff the caller (msg.sender) is an approved logger (approvedLoggers[msg.sender]); the mutant instead (incorrectly) returns true when the _requester is an approved logger, so there exist inputs where caller is unapproved but _requester approved and the return value differs.

For all inputs, logRedemptionRequested returns true exactly when the caller (msg.sender) is an approved logger; the mutant instead returns true when the _requester is approved, so there exist inputs where caller is unapproved but _requester is approved and the return value differs.

For all inputs, C.logRedemptionRequested returns true iff the caller (msg.sender) is an approved logger; the mutant returns true based on the _requester being approved, so when caller is unapproved but _requester is approved the mutant differs.

For every call to logRedemptionRequested, the reference contract returns true exactly when msg.sender is an approved logger; the mutant instead checks the _requester, so there exist inputs where msg.sender is not approved but _requester is approved and the mutant returns true while the reference returns false.
